The film, directed by [[Jon Favreau]], written by Favreau [[Dave Filoni]] and [[Noah Kloor]], and produced by Favreau, [[Kathleen Kennedy]], Filoni, and [[Ian Bryce]], takes place between the events of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']]. It continues and is a spinoff of the [[Disney+]] series [[Star Wars: The Mandalorian|''The Mandalorian'']]. In ''The Mandalorian and Grogu'', the characters of [[Din Djarin]] (the titular "[[Mandalorian]]") and [[Din Grogu|Grogu]] embark on a new adventure. The film stars [[Pedro Pascal]], reprising his role as Din Djarin, and [[Sigourney Weaver]]. [[Ludwig Göransson]], the original composer of ''The Mandalorian'', returns to score the film. The film is the first in a new slate of ''Star Wars'' films and takes place in the same timeline as the ongoing Disney+ series ''The Mandalorian'', a [[The Mandalorian Season Four|fourth season]] of which is still in development, and ''[[Star Wars: Ahsoka]]''. ==Publisher's summary== ''The Mandalorian, a lone bounty hunter, is tasked with capturing Grogu, a mysterious and adorable creature. Instead, he forms a strong bond with Grogu and strives to protect him from various threats, exploring his evolving purpose in a post-Empire galaxy.''{{WebCite|url=https://productionlist.com/production/the-mandalorian-and-grogu|text=The Mandalorian and Grogu (Feature Film)|work=[https://productionlist.com Production List]|archivedate=20240210230003}} ==Development== {{Quote|Dave Filoni and Jon Favreau have a new vision, continuing on with a Mandalorian movie.|Giancarlo Esposito|{{WebCite|url=https://www.cultureslate.com/editorials/dragon-con-qa-with-star-wars-guests-from-ahsoka-the-mandalorian-the-book-of-boba-fett-and-the-acolyte|text=Dragon Con Q&A With 'Star Wars' Guests From 'Ahsoka,' 'The Mandalorian,' 'The Book Of Boba Fett,' And 'The Acolyte’|author=Cate Feeney|date=2024-09-27|work=''Culture Slate''|archivedate=20241003035121}}}} ''The Mandalorian and Grogu'' was announced, originally as ''The Mandalorian & Grogu'', on [[January 9]], [[2024]] on [[StarWars.com]] with a conceptual sketch by veteran illustrator [[Ryan Church]], along with an announcement of a [[Ahsoka Season 2|second season]] of the television series ''[[Star Wars: Ahsoka]]''. A [[The Mandalorian Season Four|fourth season of ''The Mandalorian'']] is also reportedly still in development.{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2024/01/mandalorian-grogu-movie-jon-favreau-lucasfilm-1235700326|text='The Mandalorian & Grogu': Jon Favreau To Direct And Produce 'Star Wars' Pic For Lucasfilm|date=2024-01-09|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20240109174536}} However, series actor [[Giancarlo Esposito]] suggested the film was part of "a new vision" for ''The Mandalorian''. On [[May 7]], [[2019]], [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]] revealed their future movie release schedule, including a set of three untitled new ''Star Wars'' films, one of which had a scheduled release date of [[December 20]], 2024.{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2019/film/news/disney-avatar-star-wars-marvel-1203207661|text=Disney Moves 'Avatar' Sequels, Announces New 'Star Wars' Films|author=Brent Lang and Rebecca Rubin|date=2019-05-07|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200727083136}} ''[[The Star Wars Show]]'' also reported on the news on [[May 15]].{{StarWarsShow|dUSoopV7EKo|Star Wars Dates Announced, Plus We Won an Emmy!|sw_url=video/star-wars-dates-announced-plus-we-won-an-emmy}} On [[July 23]], [[2020]], after the onset of the [[Wikipedia:COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19 pandemic]], the film was delayed to [[December 19]], [[2025]].{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2020/film/box-office/star-wars-films-avatar-sequels-pushed-back-a-year-in-disney-release-calendar-shakeup-1234715104|text='Star Wars' Films, 'Avatar' Sequels Pushed Back a Year in Disney Release Calendar Shakeup|author=Rebecca Rubin|date=2020-07-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200723212010}} After the start of the [[Wikipedia:2023 Writers Guild of America strike|2023 Writers Guild of America strike]], Disney shifted their theatrical film release slate, with the film being pushed to its current release date of [[May 22]], [[2026]].{{SW|url=news/d23-2024-lucasfilm-reveals|text=D23 2024: All the Star Wars News from D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event}} A [[Untitled Star Wars film (Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy)|film]] directed by [[Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy]] occupied this release slot until ''The Mandalorian & Grogu'' was announced.{{TikTok|vicenews|video/7224156139078831387|Pakistan-born Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy will be the first woman and person of colour to direct one of three new Star Wars films. She's Muslim, brown, an Oscar-winning documentary filmmaker and this is her first major Hollywood feature.|archivedate=20230505000552}} [[Star Wars Insider 224|''Star Wars Insider'' 224]] revealed the initial film logo was the same as the one for [[The Mandalorian Season Three|''The Mandalorian'' Season Three]].{{InsiderCite|224|Launchpad}} Principal photography was scheduled to begin in June 2024 in [[Wikipedia:California|California]],{{WebCite|Author=Chris McPherson|date=2024-02-11|url=https://collider.com/mandalorian-and-grogu-movie-production-start|text='The Mandalorian & Grogu' Movie Eyes Summer Production Start|archivedate=20240211161755|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]}} and was expected to last for 92 days and have approximately 54 cast members, 3,500 background extras, and 500 crew members.{{WebCite|author=Dominic Patten|date=2024-02-26|text='The Mandalorian & Grogu' Lands One Of California's Largest Tax Credit Awards Ever; First 'Star Wars' Flick To Be Shot In Golden State|url=https://deadline.com/2024/02/california-film-tax-credits-mandalorian-grogu-1235838145|archivedate=20240226150433|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]}} [[David Klein]] returned as director of photography from the ''The Mandalorian''.{{WebCite|text=DAVID KLEIN, ASC - DIRECTOR OF PHOTOGRAPHY|url=https://www.davidkleinasc.com/#TheMandalorianandGrogu|archivedate=20251222231231|work=[[David Klein]]'s website}} ''The Mandalorian and Grogu'' aimed to be the first ''Star Wars'' filmed to be filmed entierly in California. During the D23 2024 on [[August 10]] of that year, it was revealed that the film had entered production several weeks prior{{WebCite|author=Tara Salvati|date=2024-08-24|text=Star Wars' Next Movie Officially Began Filming "Weeks Ago" To Hit 2026 Release|url=https://screenrant.com/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-movie-filming-start-confirmation|archivedate=20240810130141|work=[[Wikipedia:Screen Rant|''Screen Rant'']]}} and a new logo was revealed{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarsnewsnet.com/2024/08/the-mandalorian-and-grogu-now-in-production-teaser-trailer-shown-to-d23-audiences.html|text='The Mandalorian and Grogu' Now In Production, Teaser Trailer Shown To D23 Audiences|archivedate=20240810092945}} in addition to a teaser that was shown to the audience which showed the reappearance of [[Garazeb Orrelios]] from ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' and ''The Mandalorian'' season three and [[Anzellan]]s. Later that same month, [[Sigourney Weaver]] revealed that she had joined the cast of of the film, but hadn't yet started filming.{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2024/08/sigourney-weaver-interview-venice-film-festival-golden-lion-award-alien-avatar-1236052005|text=Sigourney Weaver, On Eve Of Her Venice Lifetime Achievement Award, Lifts Lid On Remarkable Career From 'Alien' To 'Avatar', 'Working Girl' To 'Ghostbusters' And 'Star Wars' Role To Come|author=Andreas Wiseman|date=2024-08-27|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20240828022426}} Additional footage was shown to audiences at D23 Brasil 2024 on [[November 9]].{{SW|url=news/d23-brasil-andor-season-2-premiere-date-announce|text=D23 Brasil 2024: ''Andor'' Premiere Date Revealed and Other ''Star Wars'' News}} Filming had wrapped by by early December.{{WebCite|author=Molly Brizell|date=2024-12-03|url=https://screenrant.com/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-finished-filming|text=Star Wars' Next Movie Has Finished Filming, Lucasfilm Boss Teases Grogu's Future|archivedate=20241203212404|work=[[Wikipedia:Screen Rant|''Screen Rant'']]}} The final writing credits, consisting of Jon Favreau & Dave Filoni & [[Noah Kloor]], were revealed by the [[Wikipedia:Writer's Guild of America West|Writer's Guild of America West]] on [[February 17]], [[2026]]. ==Release and reception== ''The Mandalorian and Grogu'' is scheduled for release on May 22, 2026. The first teaser trailer was released on [[September 22]], [[2025]]. A short advertisement, entitled "[[A New Journey Begins]]," aired during [[Wikipedia:Super Bowl LX|Super Bowl LX]] on [[February 8]], 2026,{{SW|url=news/the-mandalorian-and-grogu-big-game-spot|text=The Mandalorian and Grogu Debuts a Big Game Spot}} with another trailer was released on [[February 22]].{{SWYouTube|IHWlvwu8t1w|The Mandalorian and Grogu | Official Trailer | In Theaters May 22}} Pascal and Weaver presented the awards for [[Wikipedia:Academy Award for Best Production Design|Best Production Design]] and [[Wikipedia:Academy Award for Best Visual Effects|Best Visual Effects]] at the [[Wikipedia:98th Academy Awards|98th Academy Awards]] on [[March 15]]. Their presentation was accompanied by an appearance of Grogu seated next to actress [[Wikipedia:Kate Hudson|Kate Hudson]] in the audience.{{SWYoutube|Hu_QV1HQ2rs|The Mandalorian and Grogu | Pedro Pascal, Sigourney Weaver, Grogu & The Oscars | In Theaters May 22}} ==Adaptations and tie-in media== During D23 2024 it was also announced that alongside the release of the movie, [[Millennium Falcon: Smuggler's Run|''Millennium Falcon'': Smuggler's Run]] will be updated to include a new mission featuring Djarin, Grogu, [[Tatooine]], [[Endor]] and [[Cloud City]], which takes place off camera from the film.{{DPB|url=disney-experiences/sxsw-2025-new-missions-smugglers-run-mandalorian|text=SXSW: New Details for Mando and Grogu's Millennium Falcon Mission Revealed}} The reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian Visual Guide]]'', written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]],{{SW|url=news/nycc-2025-lucasfilm-publishing-reveals|text=NYCC 2025: All the News and Reveals from the Lucasfilm Publishing Panel}} will release prior to the film on [[April 2]], 2026 in the UK{{DK|url=uk/book/9780241791295-star-wars-the-mandalorian-visual-guide|text=Star Wars The Mandalorian Visual Guide}} and [[May 19]] in the US.{{DK|url=us/book/9798217136667-star-wars-the-mandalorian-visual-guide|text=Star Wars The Mandalorian Visual Guide}} Various other tie-ins and merchendise will also be released as part of the ''Star Wars'': "Most Wanted" campaign.{{SW|url=news/the-mandalorian-and-grogu-most-wanted-announce|text=''Star Wars:'' "Most Wanted" Campaign Unveils First Merchandise for ''The Mandalorian and Grogu''}}
